title: Clean Energy Grid Resiliency and Clean Water Modernization Act
summary: Authorizes $2.5 billion in state general obligation bonds over 10 years to reinforce electrical substation flood defenses, modernize regional high-voltage grid interconnects, and upgrade municipal wastewater treatment facilities.
yesVoteMeans: A 'YES' vote approves authorizing $2.5 billion in state general obligation bonds dedicated to public electrical grid reinforcement, battery storage pilots, and clean water treatment upgrades.
noVoteMeans: A 'NO' vote maintains current state bond authorization levels and leaves grid resilience upgrades to local utility capital budgets without dedicated state bond financing.

fiscalImpact.revenueSource: Existing state general fund revenues; does NOT create a new tax
fiscalImpact.officialSource: Washington Office of Financial Management Fiscal Note

supporters.name: Washington Clean Energy Alliance
supporters.argument: Secures essential electric transmission capacity against wildfires and extreme winter storms without raising property taxes.

supporters.name: Association of Washington Cities
supporters.argument: Provides crucial infrastructure grants to rural wastewater facilities that cannot afford capital replacements alone.

opponents.name: Taxpayers for Fiscal Prudence
opponents.argument: General obligation bonds encumber general fund debt capacity that could otherwise fund elementary education.

title: Regional Rapid Transit Expansion and Safe Crossings Levy
jurisdiction: King County / Sound Transit Service Area
summary: Renews and expands the 0.15% sales tax and creates an annual $25 motor vehicle excise tax to fund 4 new rapid bus lines, 12 grade-separated pedestrian overpasses, and discounted youth transit passes.
yesVoteMeans: A 'YES' vote approves a 0.15% local sales tax renewal and $25 vehicle fee to fund East-West rapid bus lines and pedestrian safety overpasses.
noVoteMeans: A 'NO' vote allows the existing transit levy to expire in 2027, reducing scheduled regional feeder bus expansion.

supporters.name: Transit for All Coalition
supporters.argument: Connects underserved residential neighborhoods to hospital centers and light rail terminals.

opponents.name: Fair Car Tax Association
opponents.argument: Vehicle excise fees place a disproportionate burden on working commuter families who drive to jobs without transit access.
